channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Russia to Provide Financial Aid to Kyrgyzstan for Drug Trafficking Fight
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet of Ministers has approved an agreement with Russia for financial and organizational assistance in combating illicit drug trafficking. The agreement, signed by the interior ministers of both countries in Dushanbe, outlines cooperation in fighting drug crimes. Specific funding amounts and support forms are detailed within the agreement itself.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Mountain Rescue Service Needs Systemic Overhaul After Teenager's Death
item.description: A recent tragedy where a teenager died due to a poorly organized rescue operation in Kyrgyzstan's Ala-Archa gorge highlights the urgent need for systemic reform of the mountain rescue service (MES KR). While some resources and trained personnel exist, they are insufficient. Experts suggest studying the effective systems of Switzerland, France, and Canada for potential improvements.

item.title: Heating and Hot Water Temporarily Shut Off in Part of Bishkek's Asanbay District
item.description: A section of Bishkek's Asanbay microdistrict experienced a temporary outage of heating and hot water on November 13 due to damage to the heating network. The city's mayor's office reported the disruption, affecting numerous addresses. Bishkekteploсети aims to repair the damage within the day.

item.title: Police Launch Criminal Case Over Alleged Abuse at Astana Kindergarten
item.description: Astana police have opened a criminal investigation following a complaint from a mother alleging physical abuse at state kindergarten №87 "Qadyr". The mother posted on social media, providing photos of bruises on her child. The Esil district police department is conducting the investigation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Allows Heirs to Obtain Death Certificates Based on Wills
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has expanded the list of individuals eligible to receive a death certificate, now including those with a notarized will of the deceased. President Sadyr Japarov signed the law, which amends the "Civil Status Acts" law. This change aims to simplify inheritance procedures and takes effect in three months.

item.title: Expanding Rural Areas is Necessary for National Development
item.description: The development of a nation is reflected in its citizens' quality of life, access to education, and healthcare availability, particularly in remote villages. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev emphasized the strategic importance of rural development in his address. Addressing infrastructure and sustainable income sources is crucial for retaining the rural population.

item.title: Lawyer Klara Sooronkulova Becomes 11th Candidate for Kyrgyzstan Presidential Election
item.description: Lawyer and public figure Klara Sooronkulova has submitted her application to run for president of Kyrgyzstan, becoming the 11th contender for the January 27, 2027 election. A former judge and leader of the 'Reforma' party, Sooronkulova previously ran in the 2021 presidential election. She joins ten other candidates who have also filed their applications.

item.title: Preserving National Values is Crucial for Kazakhstan's Development
item.description: A republican delegation met with residents of Turkistan to discuss priorities from the President's address to the nation. Key topics included strengthening social cohesion, fostering youth civic engagement, and promoting national values. The importance of education, integrity, and innovation for the younger generation was emphasized.

item.title: Astana to Host Counter-Terrorism Exercise on November 13
item.description: An anti-terrorism training exercise is scheduled in Astana on November 13, between 9:00 AM and 6:00 PM. The drill aims to test the readiness of law enforcement and special services in responding to terrorist threats. Temporary restrictions on pedestrian and vehicle movement are expected within the Kazakh National University of Sports.

item.title: Unemployment Among Pre-Retirees in Kazakhstan is Twice the National Average
item.description: Unemployment in Kazakhstan stands at 4.5%, but for individuals aged 55-64, it is significantly higher at 8.6%, the highest rate across all age groups. In Q3 2026, nearly 97,000 pre-retirees were seeking work, representing one-fifth of the country's unemployed. Women in this age group face higher unemployment rates.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Restrict Construction Near Oil Pipelines
item.description: Kazakhstan is enhancing digital control over construction near main oil pipelines. Local authorities will now identify protection zones in advance and deny land allocation requests in these areas. The information system 'Unified State Real Estate Cadastre' will display pipeline protection zones and minimum distances, preventing illegal construction and reducing accident risks.

item.title: Kazakhstan Discusses Forest Development and Afforestation Goals
item.description: A roundtable on "Developing Forest Potential and its Role in Achieving Ecological and Climate Goals" was held in Kazakhstan. Discussions included the current state and future tasks of forestry development. The country's forest cover has increased from 3.8% to 5.15% since 1991, with over 1.6 billion seedlings planted on more than 1 million hectares.

item.title: EAEС Business Activity Shows Positive Dynamics, Report Finds
item.description: The Eurasian Economic Commission's annual report indicates positive trends in business conditions within the EAEС. Mutual trade grew by 12.9% to $95.7 billion in the past year. The number of active legal entities and small enterprises is increasing, while unemployment is decreasing across member states.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Inspect State Bodies for Personal Data Protection Compliance
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has approved procedures for inspecting state bodies and their subordinate organizations on compliance with personal data protection laws. The measure, signed by the cabinet minister, aims to control the handling of citizens' personal information by government institutions and related entities.

item.title: Kazakh Tenge vs. Dollar: Exchange Rate Fluctuations Over Three Years
item.description: The Kazakh tenge has shown significant fluctuations against the US dollar over the past three years. After a period of depreciation, the tenge strengthened considerably in 2026, with analysts predicting a slight weakening to 490.5 tenge per dollar in 2027.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Presents 'Bishkek Arena' Stadium to Central Asian Construction Ministers
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Construction Minister Nurdin Oruntayev introduced the newly built 'Bishkek Arena' stadium to his counterparts from China, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan. The stadium, designed for 51,000 spectators, features a diameter of 280 meters and a height of 70 meters, covering 85,000 square meters. It is described as the largest football arena in Central Asia.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Present Flood Forecasting Systems at COP31 Climate Conference
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Emergency Situations will present practical solutions for flood and mudflow forecasting at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey. The event, supported by the World Bank's RESILAND CA+ project, will discuss early warning systems, digital infrastructure, and protective structures. Practical outcomes from the Kögart river basin project will be showcased.

item.title: Kazakhstan Poised to Strengthen Global Position in Critical Minerals Market
item.description: Kazakhstan has the potential to attract significant investment in the exploration, extraction, and processing of critical minerals, thereby enhancing its role in global supply chains. A Boston Consulting Group study highlights that industrial companies often underestimate the risks associated with mineral shortages.

item.title: Kazakhstan National Bank Adjusts Foreign Currency Deposit Rates
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Bank has raised the maximum interest rate on savings deposits in foreign currency from 1% to 2.5%, effective October. This marks the first revision in a decade, aiming to maintain the established balance of tenge deposits, which now constitute the majority of total deposits.

item.title: WHO Notes Kyrgyzstan's Success in Tuberculosis Fight Amid Regional Challenges
item.description: The World Health Organization reports significant progress in Kyrgyzstan's fight against tuberculosis, with incidence halved by 2024 compared to 2015. While the region shows success, drug-resistant tuberculosis remains a major threat, particularly rifampicin-resistant strains. Kyrgyzstan is included in the WHO's list of countries with a high burden of drug-resistant TB for 2026-2030.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Registered Unemployed May Drop to 27,300 by 2027
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's number of officially registered unemployed is projected to fall to approximately 27,300 by the end of 2027, according to a comparative forecast using four mathematical models. This represents a potential decrease of about 7,700 individuals from the 35,000 registered in September 2026. The registered unemployment rate has seen a significant decline since January 2021.

item.title: Traffic Restrictions in Astana Due to Anti-Terrorism Drills
item.description: Traffic will be restricted in Astana on November 13th from 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM due to anti-terrorism exercises at the Kazakh National University of Sports. Pedestrian and vehicle movement will be limited near Karkaraly Highway, 15. Residents are urged to cooperate and rely on official information.

item.title: Modern Nursery to be Built in Kyrgyzstan's Chuy Forestry Enterprise with Korean Cooperation
item.description: Construction has begun on a modern nursery at the Chuy hunting and forestry enterprise in Kyrgyzstan, as part of Kyrgyz-Korean cooperation. The project, supported by the Ministry of Natural Resources, aims to develop the national nursery system and restore forests. Representatives from both countries attended the groundbreaking ceremony.

item.title: Russian Doctors Perform Two Complex Surgeries in Osh, Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Russian doctors, as part of the "Mission of Good" volunteer program, have performed two complex surgeries in Osh, Kyrgyzstan, alongside local colleagues. Urologist Konstantin Notov and traumatologist-orthopedist Denis Zgirsky conducted operations for prostate adenoma and urinary tract stones. They are also providing consultations and masterclasses.

item.title: Tajikistan to Implement Anti-Corruption Checks on Foreign Gold Mining Agreements
item.description: Tajikistan will introduce anti-corruption expertise for agreements with foreign companies involved in gold mining. The law amendments also extend state regulation to artisanal mining and transfer illegally obtained precious metals to the state fund. President Emomali Rahmon signed the changes into law.

item.title: Coalition Sues Five Leading AI Companies Over Safety Concerns
item.description: A coalition of internet safety and consumer rights groups has filed a lawsuit against five major AI companies, including Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI, and SpaceXSI. The lawsuit, filed in San Francisco, demands a halt to further AI development, citing risks of catastrophic harm and potential existential threats to humanity.

item.title: 14 Dead, 30 Injured in Massive Pile-up in Fujairah, UAE
item.description: A major traffic accident involving 23 vehicles, including five trucks, occurred near the entrance to Fujairah, UAE. The crash resulted in 14 fatalities and 30 injuries. A truck lost control, initiating a chain reaction that led to a fire spreading across multiple vehicles. Investigations are ongoing.

item.title: Kazakhstan Detains Heads of Wealth Fund and Railway Company on Corruption Charges
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee has detained the heads of the national wealth fund Samruk-Kazyna and the state railway company KTZ on suspicion of corruption. The detentions raise concerns about corporate governance in key economic sectors and could delay the planned IPO of Kazakh Railways. The KNB has not identified other individuals taken into custody.

item.title: China Launches Extensive Information Campaign in Uzbekistan
item.description: China is conducting a broad information campaign in Uzbekistan, utilizing CGTN to promote its political, economic, and cultural ties with the country. The campaign, featuring around 70 articles and videos in Uzbek and Russian, aims to counter positive perceptions of US engagement and foster goodwill. It targets various segments of Uzbek society, highlighting opportunities for business, study, and travel.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Regional Climate Integration Initiative for Sustainable Development
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has proposed a regional climate integration model at the COP31 summit, framing climate action as a driver for economic development and regional cooperation. The initiative emphasizes "green" development and technological modernization. Uzbekistan has already achieved its target for reducing greenhouse gas emissions per unit of GDP ahead of schedule.

item.title: Uzbekistan Constitutional Court Reviews Administrative Offense Code
item.description: The Constitutional Court of Uzbekistan reviewed a complaint regarding the administrative offense code. Applicants argued that a single Supreme Court judge's decision in administrative cases lacks an appeal mechanism, contradicting constitutional rights. This issue affects individuals facing administrative charges, who are denied review rights available in other legal proceedings.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea Enhance Cooperation Against Corruption
item.description: Uzbekistan and South Korea are expanding cooperation in combating corruption. During a parliamentary delegation's visit to Seoul, Uzbek Senate Chairperson Tanzila Narbaeva met with the head of South Korea's Anti-Corruption Commission. They discussed current cooperation, reforms in Uzbekistan, and agreed to develop a plan for using digital technologies and exchanging best practices.

item.title: Turkmen Citizen Sought by US Immigration After Prison Release
item.description: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) is seeking a Turkmen citizen, Shageldy Byashimov, who overstayed his visa after being released from prison. ICE had issued a detainer for Byashimov before his May 28, 2026 release, but prison officials reportedly ignored it. The Department of Homeland Security called him a 'violent criminal,' raising concerns about public safety.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Presidential Election: Candidate Nomination Period Closes Today
item.description: The deadline for nominating candidates and submitting related documents for the presidential election in Kyrgyzstan is today, November 12, at midnight. Aspirants must submit applications and required documents to the Central Election Commission. Collecting at least 30,000 voter signatures and paying the election fee are necessary for registration.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Reviews Bukhara Refinery Modernization and Expansion Plans
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed plans for modernizing and expanding the Bukhara Oil Refinery. The refinery, operational since 1997, processes 2.5 million tons of oil annually. A $328 million project aims to produce Euro-5 compliant AI-92 and AI-95 gasoline, enhancing production capabilities and product quality.

item.title: Uzbekistan Continues Road and Bridge Repair Projects Across Regions
item.description: Road and bridge repairs and upgrades are ongoing in Uzbekistan's regions. Projects include work on major highways and local roads, with preparations underway for winter conditions. Efforts aim to improve infrastructure quality and ensure safe travel for road users.

item.title: Turkmenistan to Receive $4 Million for Renewable Energy Development
item.description: Turkmenistan and the UNDP have signed a five-year project to promote renewable energy, particularly solar power, and improve energy access in remote areas. Funded by a $4.17 million Global Environment Facility grant, the project will install up to 10 pilot solar mini-grids and assess potential for 120 more locations.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Climate Initiatives Highlighted by International Media at COP31
item.description: Foreign media outlets are covering Uzbekistan's climate initiatives presented at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. International agencies focused on the proposals for regional cooperation, combating climate change impacts, and advancing Central Asia's environmental agenda, including a regional climate integration model.

item.title: Turkmenistan's Neutrality Initiatives Drive Peace and Cooperation
item.description: Turkmenistan actively promotes global peace, stability, and regional cooperation, aligning with its 35th Independence Day celebrations. The country is advancing a peace-loving foreign policy, fostering dialogue, and realizing cooperation potential. This includes chairing the Consultative Meeting of Heads of State of Central Asian countries and Azerbaijan, and the CIS.

item.title: 13th Turkmen-German Forum Focuses on Healthcare Advancement
item.description: The 13th Turkmen-German Forum on healthcare has commenced, utilizing a digital platform. This forum aims to expand international cooperation and direct healthcare towards innovation, integrating global medical advancements into national practice. It seeks to further strengthen partnerships with German institutions.
